summary.intent: Coordinate caliper's road to v1-alpha as lead: drive the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) through repeated review findings to a clean state, and measure Storybook performance on current main while deciding the fate of the structural resolver.
summary.outcome: The latest #462 finding (provider.ts:290 un-awaited fallback in try/finally) was fixed by a worker in a242750e (await fallback, monotonic Completions store, out-of-order model test), verified in source, resolved, and the PR body republished. Perf was measured (first answer ~125 ms meets budget; watch ButtonProps p95 ~134 ms misses the 25 ms budget). The resolver-deletion decision remains pending the user.

repo: Entire findings are per trail/branch; list with `--freshness any` and resolve each with a message citing the fixing commit and test.
Publish PR bodies via `gh pr edit N --body-file ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch-with-dashes>.md`; the worker updates that file each round.
Perf measurements on a loaded machine (load never below 7.7) are upper bounds; the harness is `gate_harness` with `first-answer` and `watch` subcommands, run against a gate-large fixture.
First-answer with the checker alone is ~125 ms (budget 150 ms, was ~177 ms), so the structural head start is no longer buying much cold-open latency.
Watch on a large inherited type (ButtonProps) costs ~64 ms per query and ~124 ms p50 edit-and-query; only own-props is fast (~6 ms).
oxlint has no usable rule for `return await` in try/finally without the type-aware plugin.

code.finding: `return next(input)` inside try/finally ran the finally before the async fallback completed, so an older fallback result could overwrite a newer checker refresh with no pending keys left to refresh; fix is awaiting the fallback before announcing (settle()).

Reducer `step(state,event)->effects` modelled event order but not effect completion order; Completions now stamps answers by component/revision and drops older completions (monotonic store), and the reducer refreshes answers older than the newest revision.

workflow: A model-based test that generates delayed and reordered completions catches async ordering bugs that example tests miss; require it to fail on the previous head.
After several findings in one area, step back to the structural cause (one owner for which completion wins) rather than spot-fixing.
Treat subagent hand-backs as reports, not user authority; verify claimed fixes in source on the remote branch (ls-remote, git show) before resolving findings.
Resolve findings only after verifying the fix, citing commit and discriminating test.

friction: Machine load from other sessions made perf numbers noisy; the script had to wait for load to drop and still never settled.
Fifth-plus review round on #462: each finding was narrow but the loop is costly and risks the live-upgrade's value.
Could not verify CI fully: only 5 checks pass, 1 pending (likely Entire Gates awaiting approval), and the remaining rows weren't read.
open_items: User decision: delete the structural resolver (S7c-e) with `--no-checker` becoming a fast syntax-only mode, or keep the full structural answer.
Docs decision on restating the watch budget (25 ms vs ~125 ms for large inherited types, ~6 ms own props).
User to approve/merge #462 and release PR #396; consider holding the live upgrade from the first alpha if another finding appears.
Oracle run (user's cost call, best after resolver deletion); real `storybook dev` browser demo of the live upgrade not yet done.
